mappings.note: What achieving a great dream requires -- major personal sacrifices and financial investment, against luck or dependence on others. The cost clause of the letter's case, C-2.2-LO-38.
The journey will be an UPHILL task -- a metaphor, and the distractors (simple, normal, casual) are all literal, so what the item tests is the figure. C-2.2-LO-36.
What a person needs to survive the journey (burning conviction) -- the self-belief the letter argues for, C-2.2-LO-38. The item that asks what the phrase MEANS is mapped to LO-35 instead.
How 'burning conviction' is DEFINED -- a deep, passionate belief. The student must read 'burning' as figurative rather than literal and say what it adds, which is C-2.2-LO-35.
What keeps a person going when stamina runs out (inner motivation) -- the self-belief argument, C-2.2-LO-38.
Inner motivation comes from the simple JOY of doing what you love -- the letter's account of where persistence comes from, C-2.2-LO-38.

Which statement matches the mother's advice -- true success demands a decade of focused effort. C-2.2-LO-38, and the wrong options are all softenings of her case. DEFECT: answer trails 'Click Here to Buy book on Amazon'.
The journey is filled with CHALLENGES -- the caution half of the case, C-2.2-LO-38.
Dedication must be CONTINUOUS -- the persistence the letter argues for, C-2.2-LO-38.

The distinction between mere dreamers and actual ACHIEVERS -- the antithesis the letter is built on, which C-2.2-LO-36 names explicitly alongside metaphor and imagery. Chosen over LO-38 to mark the items that turn on the opposed pair rather than on the argument's content.

Goals that remain just 'WISHFUL thinking' -- completing a set idiom, which is what C-2.2-LO-40 covers (the idioms used in the text). Not LO-36: 'wishful thinking' is a fixed phrase, not a metaphor being analysed.
Why many abandon their dreams -- when life gets tough. The obstacle the case for self-belief has to answer, C-2.2-LO-38.
Achievers are willing to face OBSTACLES -- the letter's claim about what separates them, C-2.2-LO-38.
What achievers turn into reality (their imagination) -- the payoff the case promises, C-2.2-LO-38.

Dreamers ABANDON their dreams when life gets tough -- the negative half of the argument, C-2.2-LO-38. Kept at LO-38 rather than LO-36 because the item asks what dreamers do, not that a contrast is drawn.
What dreamers seek instead (a highly secure job) -- the retreat the letter warns against, C-2.2-LO-38.
Which statement about achievers is correct -- they are ready to invest time and make sacrifices. C-2.2-LO-38.
The distinction between the two groups is very CLEAR -- an item about the sharpness of the antithesis itself, C-2.2-LO-36.

Dreamers have wishes but avoid tough SACRIFICES -- the cost the case insists on, C-2.2-LO-38. DEFECT: page furniture is embedded inside option (D) -- 'agreements NODIA PAGE 476 CBSE CLASS 9 ENGLISH R1'.
Achievers are completely DIFFERENT from mere dreamers -- the opposed pair again, C-2.2-LO-36.

The historical event that changed her friends' lives (World War II) -- one of the anecdotes the mother uses as evidence, C-2.2-LO-38. Not C-2.1-LO-15: the item asks what the anecdote is, not how narrating differs from persuading.
Her own difficult experience (publishing a book) -- the personal evidence in the case, C-2.2-LO-38.
What the anecdotes teach -- that life is unpredictable. The conclusion drawn from the evidence, C-2.2-LO-38.
Dreams are not always PERMANENT -- the concession the letter makes while keeping its case, C-2.2-LO-38.
Dreams change and EVOLVE as a person grows -- the same concession stated positively, C-2.2-LO-38.
How the mother values Ming's evolving goals -- as worth no less than the childhood dream. The move that keeps her argument from becoming discouragement, C-2.2-LO-38.
A complex 'maze of HURDLES' -- a metaphor, with mirrors, options and rewards as the distractors. C-2.2-LO-36.

What a larger 'dreamscape' means -- more people in your support system. The student has to read the coined figurative noun rather than take it literally, C-2.2-LO-35. Not LO-36: no metaphor, antithesis or image is named, a made word is glossed.
What Ming must weigh before pursuing her dreams (the tough obstacles) -- the 'count the cost' instruction restated, C-2.2-LO-38.
